text:
The singular gaze of a gallant woman

That reaches us like the white light

The moon might send to the trembling lake

When it wishes to bathe its indolent beauty;


The last coins a gambler owns;

A lustful kiss from skinny Adeline;

The echoes of warm, enervating music,

Like the distant cry of human suffering,


None of all that is worth, oh deep bottle,

The penetrating balm that your fertile belly

Offers to the overwhelmed poet's heart;


You dispense to him life, youth, and hope

—And pride, that defense against all misery

That makes us triumphant and like gods.

translation.title: The Wine of the Solitary Man
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's comparison of sensual pleasures with wine's proud consolation.
